whatFailed: POST /v2/bookings/{uid}/reassign/{userId} answered 200 with status "success" and a reassignedTo object for a plain, non-round-robin booking, because Cal.diy replaced the removed round-robin reassignment implementation with a silent no-op stub while leaving the route, the service and the success-shaped response in place.

docClaim.quote: Currently only supports reassigning host for round robin bookings. The provided authorization header refers to the owner of the booking.
docClaim.section: reassign-a-booking-to-a-specific-host (the same sentence is the whole description of reassign-a-booking-to-auto-selected-host.md, the doc bound by the never-reached step 3). The page also publishes ReassignBookingOutput_2024_08_13 with a required status of success|error and a required data object, so a success envelope is a positive claim that a reassignment happened.

observed: Step 1 created booking uid cW2D5sw1gGqKMxAN4fbgpM on event type 100 (reference-consult, schedulingType: null in the server log, so an individual event type, and Cal.diy cannot have round-robin event types at all since teams are removed). Step 2 POSTed to /v2/bookings/cW2D5sw1gGqKMxAN4fbgpM/reassign/1 and got HTTP 200 with {"status":"success","data":{"bookingUid":"cW2D5sw1gGqKMxAN4fbgpM","reassignedTo":{"id":1,"name":"Reference Host",...}}}. reassignedTo names the host the booking already had, so nothing moved. Corroborating evidence that no work ran: the call returned in 20 ms of server time (server.stdout.txt line 359, responseTime 20) versus 6.3 s for the booking create, there is not a single log line between the incoming request and the outgoing response, and no reassignment email was even attempted (server.stderr.txt only shows the step 1 confirmation mail failing against the absent SMTP sandbox). The routes are registered: server.stdout.txt lines 174-175 map both /v2/bookings/:bookingUid/reassign and /:bookingUid/reassign/:userId at version 2024-08-13, which is the version the scenario sent, so the API-version systemic cause does not apply to this failure. Step 3 (the auto route) never ran.
impact: Silent no-op behind a false confirmation: any Cal.diy API caller with BOOKING_WRITE gets 200 success and a reassignedTo payload naming a host, while the booking is untouched. An integration that trusts the envelope believes a host handoff happened; the original host stays on the call and no one is notified. Every call to both reassign routes is affected, not just non-round-robin ones, since the feature cannot work in this edition at all.

rootCause.explanation: When the Cal.diy fork deleted packages/features/ee/round-robin/, it kept API v2's dependency on the two entry points and satisfied it with stubs: roundRobinManualReassignment (lines 126-138) and roundRobinReassignment (lines 140-150) are both empty async functions whose only body is the comment 'No-op in community edition'. apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-08-13/services/bookings.service.ts:1089-1109 awaits the stub, then re-reads the booking with getByUidWithUser and hands it to output.service.ts:539-553, which builds reassignedTo out of databaseBooking.user, i.e. the unchanged original host. bookings.controller.ts:439-468 wraps that in SUCCESS_STATUS. Nothing on the path can produce an error for the stubbed case: the service's only two catch branches translate 'invalid_round_robin_host' and 'no_available_users_found_error' thrown by the real implementation, and the stub throws neither. The same file shows the fork's own convention for this situation and shows these two stubs breaking it: createApiKeyHandler (line 162), createNewUsersConnectToOrgIfExists (198), sendVerificationCode (203) and verifyPhoneNumber (213) all throw 'X is not available in community edition', and verifyCodeAuthenticated returns a safe false. Only the two reassignment stubs return a silent success. The honest fix is to make them throw the community-edition error (which the service would surface as a 500, or better, to raise a 501 or 400 in the service) or to unregister the two routes.

notes: Read this before filing anything upstream, because the scenario is right about the outcome and wrong about the reason. (1) The scenario's premise, that a non-round-robin booking must be refused, is not what the code proves and should not be reported to cal.com. The pre-fork implementation (git show ab21c7f805^:packages/features/ee/round-robin/roundRobinManualReassignment.ts) has no schedulingType or ROUND_ROBIN gate at all: it throws invalid_round_robin_host only when the target user is not among the event type's hosts, and user_is_round_robin_fixed when the matched host is fixed. For an individual event type it falls back to eventType.users, so reassigning to the booking's own single host (userId 1, exactly what step 2 did) would have passed both checks on real cal.com too. The doc sentence 'Currently only supports reassigning host for round robin bookings' is a capability caveat, not a documented error contract, and the pages name no status code. A stricter scenario would reassign to a user who is NOT a host of the event type, which is the case the real implementation genuinely refuses. (2) What makes this a defect anyway is independent of the round-robin question: on Cal.diy the endpoint can never do anything, for any booking, and it reports success with a reassignedTo object regardless. That violates the tested tree's own contract, since bookings.controller.ts:439-450 still carries the cal.com @ApiOperation description and the ReassignBookingOutput_2024_08_13 DTO still promises a reassignment. (3) On the edition-mismatch question: the underlying feature is genuinely EE-removed (README line 47 lists Teams among the removed enterprise features, and the whole packages/features/ee/round-robin/ directory was deleted in #28903), so a reviewer could stop at edition-mismatch. It is not one, per the brief's own rule, because Cal.diy does ship the code on this path and that code misbehaves: the fork chose a silent no-op where its own four sibling stubs in the same file throw 'not available in community edition'. That deviation, in packages/platform/libraries/index.ts:126-150, is the one-line actionable report for a Cal.diy maintainer. (4) Step 3, the auto route, never ran, but roundRobinReassignment at lines 140-150 is the identical no-op, so it would have returned success the same way; the failure is representative of both bound doc pages. (5) The API-version systemic cause does not apply here: the docs demand cal-api-version 2026-02-25, but the scenario sent 2024-08-13, which Cal.diy really has, and the router log confirms both routes were matched at that version.
